about: Synthetic benchmark of subscription-rotation policies. Simulated; plan limits are made-up tiers in relative units.
assumptions: 1 plan unit is one weekly allowance of a small personal plan; the other plan tiers are made-up multiples of it.

Each seed jitters each plan limit by up to ±25% and places the weekly resets: at random minutes of the week (resets: random), or evenly spaced from a random start in a random account order (resets: even).
Work is interchangeable across providers: an agent task can run on either.
Demand intensity is demand per measured week divided by the accounts' combined weekly allowance; it is exact in every seed.
Steady-state cells start with every weekly allowance spent and measure after the warm-up. The after-a-break cell starts with every account unused and measures from the start.

demandModels.keeps-blasting: Steady demand 16 hours a day (07:00-23:00), 7 days a week
demandModels.agents-24-7: Steady demand around the clock (agents never stop)
demandModels.bursty: Random work sessions (about 1.5 h on, 2 h off) during waking hours
demandModels.uneven-days: Waking-hours demand whose level changes day to day (uniform 0-2x the mean)
demandModels.busy-weeks-then-quiet: Three busy weeks of waking-hours work, then a quiet week with nothing sent
demandModels.sprint-weeks: A sprint week at 1.6x the mean, then a light week at 0.4x, waking hours
demandModels.weekdays: Busy weekdays 07:00-23:00, quiet weekends with nothing sent

policies.rule: 5-hour accounts with room first, then the soonest weekly reset (src/rotation.mjs, 15-minute hold)
policies.round-robin: Per-request rotation over the accounts with room; a full account drops out and the others split its share
policies.random: A fresh random order every minute, failing over to the next account with room
policies.fixed-order: One order per seed, drawn at random, failing over to the next account with room
